headline: Notre-Dame's roof burned in April, a million marched in Hong Kong in June, the House impeached Trump in December
texture: The Walt Disney Company completed its purchase of 21st Century Fox on March 20 and took operational control of Hulu on May 14, leaving Comcast a 33 percent stake it can be made to sell. CBS and Viacom agreed on December 4 to merge back into one company after thirteen years apart. Bungie ended its publishing deal with Activision on January 10 and kept Destiny. Nintendo shut the Wii Shop Channel on January 30, twelve years after it opened.

Maine banned polystyrene food containers on May 1. Denver voted 51 to 49 on May 8 to decriminalise psychedelic mushrooms, San Francisco banned city use of facial recognition six days later, and Washington state legalised human composting on May 21. Sandusky, Ohio had already made Election Day a paid holiday on January 30 by dropping Columbus Day to pay for it. A blackout on Manhattan's West Side on July 13 cut power to 73,000 customers, exactly 42 years after the one in 1977.

The last Volkswagen Beetle came off the line in Puebla on July 10, the last of 5,961 Special Edition cars. October 25 was the last day tourists could climb Uluru, before the ban took effect. About a hundred Icelanders held a funeral on August 18 for Okjokull, a glacier that had covered 15.5 square kilometres. Thomas Cook went bankrupt on September 23 and stranded 600,000 travellers. Japan resumed commercial whaling on July 1 after a thirty-year moratorium, and India banned triple talaq on July 30.

Country House won the Kentucky Derby on May 4 as a longshot, after Maximum Security crossed the line first and was disqualified, and a twenty-third horse had died at Santa Anita racetrack by March 31. Nia Franklin, Cheslie Kryst and Kaliegh Garris held Miss America, Miss USA and Miss Teen USA at once, the first time all three winners were black women. Two of the Flying Wallendas walked a quarter-mile tightrope twenty-five storeys above Times Square on June 23.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: Mike Pence was vice president and John Roberts chief justice. Nancy Pelosi replaced Paul Ryan as Speaker of the House on January 3, and Mitch McConnell stayed Senate majority leader. Trump delivered the State of the Union address on February 5.

pol.us_congress.label: US Congress
pol.us_congress.value: 116th Congress, Democratic House and Republican Senate
pol.us_congress.detail: It opened on January 3, when the Democrats took control of the House with a promise to end the government shutdown but without funding for the border wall, and the Republicans increased their hold on the Senate.

pol.shutdown.label: Government shutdown
pol.shutdown.value: The shutdown that had begun the previous December became the longest in US history on January 12, at 22 days, with 800,000 federal employees unpaid
pol.shutdown.detail: Flights into LaGuardia were halted on January 25 for want of air traffic control staff. Trump agreed the same day to back a deal funding federal agencies for three weeks, which ended the shutdown for the time being.

pol.mueller_report.label: Mueller report delivered
pol.mueller_report.value: Robert Mueller turned in the report of his nearly two-year investigation into whether the Trump campaign helped Russia interfere in the 2016 presidential election
pol.mueller_report.detail: Attorney General William Barr sent Congress a four-page letter outlining its principal conclusions on March 24, and a redacted version of the full report was released to Congress and the public on April 18. Roger Stone had been charged on January 25 with seven counts arising from the investigation, and was found guilty of all seven on November 15.

pol.impeachment.label: Impeachment of the president
pol.impeachment.value: The House voted largely along party lines to send the Senate two articles of impeachment against Donald Trump, for abuse of power and obstruction of Congress
pol.impeachment.detail: Nancy Pelosi announced the inquiry on September 24, the White House released details of a July 25 call between Trump and the president of Ukraine the next day, and the first public hearings opened on November 13 with Bill Taylor and George Kent. The US year page calls Trump the fourth president to face impeachment.

pol.mass_shootings.label: El Paso and Dayton shootings
pol.mass_shootings.value: 23 people were killed at a Walmart near the Cielo Vista Mall in El Paso on August 3, and ten more including the gunman in the Oregon Historic District of Dayton the next morning
pol.mass_shootings.detail: The Gun Violence Archive counted 410 mass shooting incidents to December 27 and 38,820 gun deaths in all, of which 23,826 were suicides. ABC News counted 21 deadly mass shootings and 124 killed to September 30. Twenty-three states and the District of Columbia passed 70 gun safety laws in the legislative session.

world.uk_politics.label: United Kingdom
world.uk_politics.value: Boris Johnson became prime minister on July 24 after beating Jeremy Hunt in the Conservative leadership contest, and won a Commons majority of 80 seats on December 12
world.uk_politics.detail: Theresa May announced her resignation on May 24 and gave up the party leadership on June 7. Parliament was prorogued on September 10 amid protests from opposition MPs who held up signs in the Commons, and the Supreme Court ruled the prorogation unlawful and void on September 24. An estimated one million people marched through London on October 19 to demand a second referendum on Brexit.

world.hong_kong.label: Hong Kong protests
world.hong_kong.value: More than a million people marched on June 9 against a bill allowing extradition to mainland China, the largest protest in the city since the handover
world.hong_kong.detail: Hong Kong announced on June 15 that the bill was suspended indefinitely, and Carrie Lam withdrew it on September 4. A mob of over a hundred men in white attacked commuters at Yuen Long station on July 21, the airport closed on August 12, a protester was shot in the chest with a live round on October 1, and police used tear gas and water cannon at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University from November 17.

world.notre_dame.label: Notre-Dame fire
world.notre_dame.value: A fire during Holy Week brought down the roof and the main spire of Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris

world.christchurch.label: Christchurch mosque shootings
world.christchurch.value: 51 people were killed and 50 injured in attacks on two mosques, the deadliest mass shooting and terrorist attack in New Zealand's history

world.sri_lanka.label: Sri Lanka Easter bombings
world.sri_lanka.value: Islamist bombs went off at eight places on Easter Sunday, three churches, four hotels and a housing complex in Colombo, leaving 259 dead and over 500 injured
world.sri_lanka.detail: The year page calls it the deadliest terrorist attack in the country since the civil war.

world.amazon_fires.label: Amazon rainforest fires
world.amazon_fires.value: Brazil's National Institute for Space Research reported fires burning in the rainforest at a record rate, more than 36,000 in the year to that point, with smoke reaching Sao Paulo
world.amazon_fires.detail: Angela Merkel and Emmanuel Macron called the fires an international emergency on August 23 and pressed for them to be raised at that weekend's G7 summit.

world.isis.label: Islamic State
world.isis.value: The group lost its last territory at Al-Baghuz Fawqani in Syria on March 23, and Trump announced on October 27 that its leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi had died during a US special forces operation
world.isis.detail: Al-Baghdadi had appeared on April 29 in undated footage released by the group, his first video since 2014. He is reported to have set off a suicide vest after being chased into a tunnel.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, worldwide gross
value: Avengers: Endgame, $2,799,439,100, Disney
The Lion King, $1,656,943,394, Disney
Frozen 2, $1,450,026,933, Disney
Spider-Man: Far From Home, $1,131,927,996, Sony
Captain Marvel, $1,128,274,794, Disney
film.gross.detail: Worldwide gross rather than domestic, which is what the film page's table header and the sentence above it both say, citing Box Office Mojo. Disney distributed seven of the top ten and became the first studio to pass $10 billion in worldwide grosses in a single year. Toy Story 4, The Lion King and Frozen 2 each passed a billion dollars, the first time three animated films had done that in one year. Joker was sixth on $1,078,751,311 and the only one of the top nine not from Disney or Sony.

film.endgame_record.label: Avengers: Endgame passed Avatar
film.endgame_record.value: It passed Avatar to become the highest-grossing film of all time
film.endgame_record.detail: The film page cites a Hollywood Reporter piece dated July 20 for the record. The total is reported on more than one basis and this file resolves none of them: the film page's table gives $2,799,439,100 from Box Office Mojo, while the film's own article puts $2.799 billion in its infobox and calls it nearly $2.8 billion in its lead. Every one of those figures includes a re-release that opened in 1,040 United States cinemas on June 28 with seven minutes of new footage after the credits, so none is what the original run took.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.value: Parasite, produced by Kwak Sin-ae and Bong Joon-ho
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded the following February at the 92nd Academy Awards, and the first film not in English to win. Its four awards tied it with Fanny and Alexander and Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon as the most-decorated foreign language films in Academy history, and it was the twelfth Best Picture winner with no acting nomination. Joker led the field with eleven nominations, and The Irishman, 1917 and Once Upon a Time in Hollywood tied on ten each, the first time four films had reached ten in one year.

film.acting_awards.label: Acting Oscars
value: Best Actor, Joaquin Phoenix, Joker
Best Actress, Renee Zellweger, Judy
Best Supporting Actor, Brad Pitt, Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
Best Supporting Actress, Laura Dern, Marriage Story
film.acting_awards.detail: Bong Joon-ho took Best Director for Parasite and collected four statuettes in the evening, counting the international feature award he accepted on behalf of South Korea, the first person to do that for a single film. Phoenix and Heath Ledger became the second pair of actors to win for playing the same character in different films. Hildur Gudnadottir won Best Original Score for Joker, the third woman to win it and the first for a dramatic score. Scarlett Johansson was the twelfth actor nominated twice for acting in the same year.

film.world_cinema.label: Nominated for Best International Feature Film
value: Parasite, South Korea, in Korean, directed by Bong Joon-ho, the winner
Corpus Christi, Poland, in Polish, directed by Jan Komasa
Honeyland, North Macedonia, in Turkish and Macedonian, directed by Tamara Kotevska and Ljubomir Stefanov
Les Miserables, France, in French, directed by Ladj Ly
Pain and Glory, Spain, in Spanish, directed by Pedro Almodovar
film.world_cinema.detail: The Academy voted in April to rename the category, dropping Best Foreign Language Film because its committee found the word foreign outdated, while keeping the rule that most of the dialogue be in a language other than English. Honeyland was the first film nominated here and for Best Documentary Feature at once. The film page gives the festival prizes: the Palme d'Or at the 72nd Cannes Film Festival to Parasite, the Golden Lion at the 76th Venice International Film Festival to Todd Phillips's Joker, and the Golden Bear at the 69th Berlin International Film Festival to Nadav Lapid's Synonyms.

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a cinema first, except that two of the nine Best Picture nominees came from Netflix and carried no box office figure at all, because the company will not publish them
film.how_people_watched.detail: The Oscars page says grosses for The Irishman and Marriage Story were unavailable for that reason. Of the seven nominees that had figures, the seven together had taken $747.2 million at the American and Canadian box office by the time nominations were announced, Joker $334 million of it and Parasite $25.4 million.

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, season starting autumn 2019
value: Sunday Night Football, NBC, 20.09
NCIS, CBS, 15.34
Thursday Night Football, FOX, 15.05
FBI, CBS, 12.55
Blue Bloods, CBS, 11.96
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season, so this ranking covers the season that opened in the autumn and ran into the following spring. The source heads its column Rating and states no unit for the figures. Chicago Fire was sixth on 11.70, This Is Us seventh on 11.55, Young Sheldon eighth on 11.45, Chicago P.D. ninth on 11.23 and Chicago Med tenth on 11.22. None of the ten cached pages for the year carries a Nielsen table, so this comes from the by-season list instead.

tv.endings.label: Programs that ended
value: Veep, HBO, May 12, on air since 2012
The Big Bang Theory, CBS, May 16, on air since 2007
Game of Thrones, HBO, May 19, on air since 2011
Orange Is the New Black, Netflix, July 26, on air since 2013
tv.endings.detail: The Game of Thrones finale drew 13.6 million viewers, the most watched episode of any HBO show. Dates and start years come from the television page's table of shows ending in the year.

tv.emmys.label: 71st Primetime Emmy Awards
tv.emmys.value: The final season of Game of Thrones won Outstanding Drama Series and Fleabag Outstanding Comedy Series, beating the favourites Veep and The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel
tv.emmys.detail: Broadcast on Fox with no host, the fourth hostless ceremony in its history. Phoebe Waller-Bridge also won lead actress and writing in a comedy for Fleabag. Billy Porter of Pose became the first openly gay black man to win lead actor in a drama. British programmes took two of the three major awards for the first time, Fleabag and the limited series Chernobyl. The telecast pulled a 5.7 household rating in metered markets, down 23 percent on the previous year and the biggest fall of any major awards show that year, against Sunday Night Football.

tv.streaming.label: Disney+ launched
tv.streaming.value: The service went live on November 12
tv.streaming.detail: Disney and Comcast had struck a deal on May 14 giving Disney operational control of Hulu immediately, with Comcast keeping a 33 percent stake it can be required to sell at fair market value. Netflix cancelled The Punisher, whose last episodes went up on January 18, and Jessica Jones.

tv.wheel_of_fortune.label: Vanna White hosted Wheel of Fortune
tv.wheel_of_fortune.value: The first time a woman had hosted the game show since its debut in 1975
tv.wheel_of_fortune.detail: She had been co-host and letter turner since 1982. She stood in for Pat Sajak, who was recovering from surgery for a blocked intestine and missed two weeks of taping.

music.hot100_year_end.label: Year-end Hot 100 number one
music.hot100_year_end.value: Old Town Road, Lil Nas X featuring Billy Ray Cyrus
music.hot100_year_end.detail: It broke the record for the most weeks at number one in the chart's history at eighteen, with a nineteenth clocked before the Billy Ray Cyrus remix came out and credited to Lil Nas X alone. Sunflower by Post Malone and Swae Lee came second and Without Me by Halsey third. Post Malone was the year's top Hot 100 artist with five songs on the list, and Cardi B had six, more than anyone else.

music.listening_format.label: How people listened
music.listening_format.value: Billboard built the Hot 100 from physical and digital single sales, radio airplay and streaming together, compiled by Nielsen SoundScan
music.listening_format.detail: The year-end list was published on December 5 from data running from November 24, 2018 to November 16. No cached page for the year names a subscription streaming service or gives a sales figure for any format, so nothing here says what anyone played the music on.

music.grammys.label: 61st Grammy Awards
music.grammys.value: Kacey Musgraves won Album of the Year for Golden Hour and four awards in all, and This Is America by Childish Gambino took Record and Song of the Year
music.grammys.detail: Broadcast on CBS from the Staples Center in Los Angeles with Alicia Keys hosting, back in the city after a year in New York. Dua Lipa won Best New Artist. The awards honoured the previous year's recordings.

music.rock_hall.label: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductees
value: The Cure
Def Leppard
Janet Jackson
Stevie Nicks
Radiohead
Roxy Music
The Zombies
music.rock_hall.detail: The music page gives no ceremony date.

music.eurovision.label: Eurovision Song Contest
music.eurovision.value: Duncan Laurence won for the Netherlands with Arcade, at the contest held in Tel Aviv from May 14 to 18

tech.black_hole.label: First image of a black hole
tech.black_hole.value: The Event Horizon Telescope project released the first image of a black hole, at the centre of the M87 galaxy
tech.black_hole.detail: The science page puts the galaxy 54 million light years away, and records that Science named the image its breakthrough of the year on December 19.

tech.quantum_supremacy.label: Google claims quantum supremacy
tech.quantum_supremacy.value: Google said its 53-qubit Sycamore processor had done a specific task in 200 seconds that would take the best supercomputers 10,000 years

tech.spaceflight.label: Spaceflight
value: Chang'e 4 landed on the far side of the Moon on January 3, the first artificial object to do so
New Horizons made a close approach to the Kuiper belt object Arrokoth on January 1
An uncrewed SpaceX Dragon docked itself to the International Space Station on March 3
Chandrayaan-2 reached lunar orbit on September 6, but its Vikram lander crashed into the surface
Jessica Meir and Christina Koch made the first all-female spacewalk on October 18
tech.spaceflight.detail: SpaceIL launched the Beresheet probe on February 21, the world's first privately financed Moon mission. Astronomers announced on September 11 that they had detected water in the atmosphere of the exoplanet K2-18b, the first such find for a planet in the habitable zone around a star.

tech.boeing_max.label: Boeing 737 MAX grounded
tech.boeing_max.value: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crashed shortly after takeoff from Addis Ababa on March 10, killing all 157 people on board, and every 737 MAX in the world was grounded within days
tech.boeing_max.detail: The US year page dates Boeing's grounding of its entire global fleet to March 13, on the evidence gathered from the crash site, and its announcement that it would suspend production of the aircraft to December 16, with the suspension itself falling the following month.

tech.social_platforms.label: Regulators and the platforms
tech.social_platforms.value: The Federal Trade Commission approved a record $5 billion fine on Facebook, by a 3 to 2 vote, to settle an investigation into data privacy violations
tech.social_platforms.detail: The commission threatened YouTube and Google with up to $170 million on September 4 over collecting personal information from children under 13. Twitter banned political advertising worldwide on October 30. Facebook had banned Louis Farrakhan, Alex Jones and others from Facebook and Instagram on May 2, designating them dangerous individuals and organizations.

tech.games.label: Video games
value: Apex Legends, Respawn and Electronic Arts, surprise-released February 4, 25 million players inside a week
Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, FromSoftware and Activision, March 22, Game of the Year at The Game Awards on December 12
Resident Evil 2, Capcom, January 25, Game of the Year at the 37th Golden Joystick Awards on November 16
Disco Elysium, ZA/UM, October 15
tech.games.detail: SuperData put the industry at $120.1 billion worldwide, up 4 percent, of which $64.4 billion was mobile, $29.6 billion computer and $15.4 billion console. All ten of the year's highest-grossing games were free to play and each took more than a billion dollars, Fortnite most of all at $3,709,000,000. Google revealed Stadia on March 19 and launched it on November 19. Nintendo released the Switch Lite on September 20, and Valve the Index headset on June 28.

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Unleaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31.

prices.unemployment.label: US unemployment rate
prices.unemployment.value: 3.9 percent in January, 3.5 percent in November
prices.unemployment.detail: The US year page says the 3.5 percent reported on December 6 was the lowest in 50 years, and that the economy started and ended a decade without a recession for the first time in the country's history.

prices.stocks.label: US stock market at the close of the year
prices.stocks.value: The S&P 500 finished at 3,230.78, the Nasdaq Composite at 8,972.60 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average at 28,534.44
prices.stocks.detail: The S&P rose more than 28 percent, the best annual gain in six years. The Dow passed 27,000 points for the first time on July 11. The main Treasury yield curve inverted on August 13, with two-year yields above ten-year ones, and the Dow fell more than 500 points the next day on the strength of that.

prices.interest_rate.label: Federal Reserve interest rate
prices.interest_rate.value: Cut on July 31 for the first time since 2008, by 0.25 percent, to a baseline of 2 to 2.25 percent
prices.interest_rate.detail: Two more cuts followed, the last on October 30 taking the benchmark to a range of 1.5 to 1.75 percent, the third in four months. Interest rates on repurchase agreements had spiked without warning on September 17.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: A spring spent watching a cathedral roof burn live on television, a summer of weekly marches in Hong Kong that nobody could see the end of, and an autumn of impeachment hearings most people had made up their minds about before the witnesses sat down.

culture.nobel_prizes.label: Nobel Prizes
value: Literature, Peter Handke
Peace, Abiy Ahmed
Physics, James Peebles, Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz
Chemistry, John B. Goodenough, M. Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino
Physiology or Medicine, William Kaelin Jr., Peter J. Ratcliffe and Gregg L. Semenza
Economics, Abhijit Banerjee, Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer
culture.nobel_prizes.detail: The chemistry prize was for work on lithium batteries and the medicine prize for how cells sense and adapt to the oxygen available to them. The peace prize went to Ethiopia's prime minister. The year page gives no dates.

culture.climate_strike.label: Global climate strike
culture.climate_strike.value: Six million people in 4,500 locations across 150 countries struck three days before the UN Climate Action Summit, one of the largest climate mobilizations on record
culture.climate_strike.detail: A second round on September 27 put 500,000 on the streets of Montreal behind Greta Thunberg and Justin Trudeau, with four million striking worldwide. The US year page adds that Thunberg had reached New York Harbor on August 28 after sailing the Atlantic rather than flying, and that Time named her Person of the Year on December 11.

culture.area_51.label: Storm Area 51
culture.area_51.value: A proposed invasion of the classified Air Force base by two million truth-seekers fell short of its goal by about 1,999,970 people
culture.area_51.detail: The US year page says only the Pentagon took it seriously, threatening to bomb participants before apologising.

sports.super_bowl.label: Super Bowl LIII
sports.super_bowl.value: New England Patriots 13, Los Angeles Rams 3, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta in front of 70,081
sports.super_bowl.detail: Julian Edelman was named most valuable player. The US year page says Tom Brady's sixth championship was the most won by any single player, and that the Patriots' six titles tied the Steelers for the most by a team.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: Washington Nationals beat the Houston Astros four games to three, a first title for the club
sports.world_series.detail: The sports page dates the series October 22 to 30. Houston had won the American League regular season and the Los Angeles Dodgers the National League. The American League took the All-Star Game 4 to 3 at Progressive Field in Cleveland on July 9, with Shane Bieber named most valuable player, and Pete Alonso of the Mets won the Home Run Derby.

sports.champions.label: Other championships
value: NBA Finals, Toronto Raptors over the Golden State Warriors in six games, a first title, decided June 13
Stanley Cup, St. Louis Blues over the Boston Bruins in seven games, a first cup, decided June 12
UEFA Champions League, Liverpool beat Tottenham Hotspur 2 to 0 at the Metropolitano Stadium on June 1, a sixth title, with goals from Mohamed Salah and Divock Origi
Cricket World Cup, England beat New Zealand in a final that finished level and went to a Super Over that also finished level, decided on boundaries, 26 to 17
Rugby World Cup, South Africa beat England in the final, at a tournament held in Japan from September 20 to November 2
sports.champions.detail: The NBA and cricket results come from the sports page, the Stanley Cup from the US year page, and the Champions League and rugby from the world year page. Zion Williamson went first in the NBA draft on June 20, to New Orleans. The cricket tournament had run in England, with one match in Wales, since May 30.

sports.womens_world_cup.label: FIFA Women's World Cup
sports.womens_world_cup.value: The United States won a fourth title, at a tournament held in France from June 7 to July 7
sports.womens_world_cup.detail: The US year page says the team defended its position as the top-ranked side in the world and renewed its campaign for pay equity off the back of the win. Sports Illustrated named Megan Rapinoe its Sportsperson of the Year on December 9.

sports.masters.label: Masters Tournament
sports.masters.value: Tiger Woods won at Augusta National, a fifth Masters, a fifteenth major and an 81st PGA Tour win
sports.masters.detail: Played April 11 to 14. Brooks Koepka took the PGA Championship at Bethpage Black in May, Gary Woodland the US Open at Pebble Beach in June, and Shane Lowry the Open Championship at Royal Portrush in July. Woods was given the Presidential Medal of Freedom on May 6.

sports.russia_ban.label: Russia banned from international sport
sports.russia_ban.value: The World Anti-Doping Agency voted unanimously to bar the country from international sport for four years over doping offences

deaths.morrison.label: Toni Morrison
deaths.morrison.detail: American novelist, awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993 and the Pulitzer Prize for Beloved in 1988. She died at Montefiore Medical Center in the Bronx. None of the ten cached pages for the year mentions her, so this fact cites her own article.

deaths.day.label: Doris Day
deaths.day.detail: American actress and singer. The film page names Pillow Talk and The Man Who Knew Too Much.

deaths.fonda.label: Peter Fonda
deaths.fonda.detail: American actor, screenwriter and director. The film page names Easy Rider and Ulee's Gold.

deaths.perry.label: Luke Perry
deaths.perry.detail: American actor. The film page names The Fifth Element and Buffy the Vampire Slayer.

deaths.baker.label: Ginger Baker
deaths.baker.detail: British rock and jazz drummer, of Cream, Blind Faith, Ginger Baker's Air Force and The Graham Bond Organisation.

deaths.hussle.label: Nipsey Hussle
deaths.hussle.detail: American rapper. The music page gives the date and the age and no cause of death, so none is stated here.

notes: Research pass July 2026, from the ten cached wikitext pages under .sources/2019 plus three dedicated articles pulled where the cache fell short. Box office basis. bo.mjs reports GROSS and WORLDWIDE from a header reading Rank, Title, Distributor, Worldwide gross, and the sentence above the table reads the top films released in 2019 by worldwide gross, citing Box Office Mojo, so figures_basis is gross and film.gross names worldwide in both its label and its detail. Endgame and Avatar. film.endgame_record states the disagreement rather than resolving it: the film page's table gives $2,799,439,100, the film's own article gives $2.799 billion in its infobox and nearly $2.8 billion in its lead, and all of those include the re-release that opened in 1,040 United States cinemas on June 28 with seven minutes of added footage. The film page cites a Hollywood Reporter piece of July 20 for the record itself. Avatar's own figure is nowhere in the cache and is not stated here. Dedicated articles pulled, and why. Three. (1) Toni Morrison, because none of the ten cached pages mentions her at all and a 2019 page without her death is a hole a reader would notice; her article supplies the date, the age, the hospital, the 1993 Nobel and the 1988 Pulitzer. (2) Avengers: Endgame, for the re-release detail and the second reported basis for its worldwide total. (3) Top-rated United States television programs by season, because the manifest records Top-rated_United_States_television_programs_of_2019-20 as a 404 and no cached page carries a Nielsen table; that article's 2019-20 table heads its column Rating and states no unit, which tv.top_shows says outright rather than calling the figures a household rating or a viewer count. Date checks. No US federal election or presidential inauguration falls this year. February 3 was a Sunday for Super Bowl LIII, June 9 a Sunday for the first million-person Hong Kong march, and December 18 a Wednesday for the impeachment vote, all consistent with the pages. The 92nd Academy Awards ceremony falls in the following February and is written that way rather than dated, per the corpus convention, as is the fact that the Best Picture award honours this year of film. No cached page disagreed with another on a date, so no dedicated article was pulled for date checking. Nothing in this file reaches into the following year. Left out for that reason: the 92nd Academy Awards ceremony date and its nomination announcement, the 77th Golden Globes, the 25th Critics' Choice Awards, the 73rd BAFTAs, the 72nd Primetime Emmys, the 23rd D.I.C.E. Awards, the 20th Game Developers Choice Awards, the 16th British Academy Games Awards, the whole Democratic presidential primary field and every candidacy announcement and withdrawal on the US year page, the Senate impeachment trial, and the suspension date of 737 MAX production, which tech.boeing_max writes as the following month. The WADA ban on Russia is written as four years from international sport with no edition of any tournament named, per the host-city convention, because the year page lists three future events by name. COVID-19. The world year page carries a December 1 entry for a first known human case in Wuhan and a December 31 entry for the first official reports of viral pneumonia from the Wuhan Municipal Health Commission. Both are left out. Neither was a public event of 2019 in any sense a reader of this page would recognise, and any mention would carry a meaning the year did not have. Music format. music.listening_format claims only what the Billboard year-end page says about how the Hot 100 was compiled, because no cached page names Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music or any subscription service, gives a vinyl or streaming figure, or says anything else about playback. Dropped for lack of a source. 5G, TikTok, any Netflix subscriber count, any smartphone release and any Apple TV+ launch date appear nowhere in the ten cached pages, so there is no device fact and no second streaming launch beyond Disney+. No cached page ranks or counts websites, publishes a Merriam-Webster or dictionary word list for the year, or describes a meme, so culture.slang, culture.memes and tech.web_sites are all open and all empty.
